main_body: A wooden rack frame holding five kegs (three below, two above) drawn end-on, with their round faces toward the viewer. A brown plank band runs across the top, and grey-blue shadow slots sit behind the kegs.
top_band: Rows 8-13 are a graded brown plank band (dark #9a5435, then #b77246, then light #d59147 at rows 12-13). It reads as the front face of a horizontal beam, not a top surface. Nothing separates it from the face below by a clear step.
evidence: The scan at x=16 shows rows 8-12 as a thin gradient of 1-2 row steps that reads as a beam face. Below it the kegs show only vertical end discs with bands and bungs. No keg shows a top surface or a visible horizontal side. The bottom rail (rows 29-30) is a 1-2px line with no top face. The beams and base have no visible top faces, so this is an end-on front elevation and fails the frame requirement.

style.evidence: The outline is mostly tinted brown (only 6% of dark edge pixels are neutral), which matches Beodeul. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. The kegs have some shading, with hoops and bung highlights. The candidate has only 13 distinct colours against 38-40 in both references, so its palette is much thinner. Median colours per tile is 13 against 17 and 20. Each material (wood, kegs, iron) has only about 3-4 tones, and the plank band is a simple gradient with little grain. Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter, so it fails when in doubt.
